raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

K2 Horizon often closes `medium`/`low` thinking with `</ifm|think>` (the `high` end tag), but `K2HorizonReasoningParser` only looks for the end tag of the requested `reasoning_effort`. This PR treats any of the three K2 Horizon end tags as the end of reasoning, and ends reasoning at the earliest boundary, so an end tag inside a tool call that has already started no longer moves the split.

Fixes #62743. Related: #60969 (see Details).

## Claims

- With `reasoning_effort` `medium` or `low`, output closed by `</ifm|think>` is split into `reasoning` and `content` in both streaming and non-streaming. Before, non-streaming put the reasoning, the literal `</ifm|think>` and the answer in `content`, and streaming put the whole answer in `reasoning`.
- Reasoning ends at the earliest end tag or `<ifm|tool_calls>`. When the tool-call start comes first, the whole tool block stays in `content`, even if its text contains an end tag (for example a tool argument with `</ifm|think>`), and the result no longer depends on how the stream is chunked. On `main` the review example was already wrong for `high` (non-streaming and multi-token deltas split inside the tool call and lost it); the first commit of this PR extended it to `medium`/`low`.
- `is_reasoning_end`, `is_reasoning_end_streaming` and `extract_content_ids` use the same set of end tokens as extraction, so the structured-output gate agrees with the frontend about where an explicit end is.
- Output closed by the effort's own end tag parses as before. The start token is still chosen by effort.

## Validation

**Unit tests.** `test_any_effort_end_token_closes_reasoning` checks the cross-effort end tags. `test_earliest_boundary_ends_reasoning` covers all three efforts with `plan<ifm|tool_calls>…{"text":"</ifm|think>"}…` (tool call first) and `plan</ifm|think><ifm|tool_calls>…` (end tag first). Each case runs non-streaming extraction, streaming as one delta, one character at a time and split inside `<ifm|tool_calls>`, and `extract_content_ids`.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/reasoning/test_k2_horizon_reasoning_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_k2_horizon_tool_parser.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/reasoning
pre-commit run --files vllm/reasoning/k2_horizon_reasoning_parser.py tests/reasoning/test_k2_horizon_reasoning_parser.py
```

| Parser | `test_k2_horizon_reasoning_parser.py` |
|---|---|
| `main` | `5 failed, 20 passed`: the two cross-effort cases, `tool-call-first-high`, and `end-token-first` for `medium` and `low` |
| First commit of this PR | `3 failed, 22 passed`: `tool-call-first` for `high`, `medium` and `low` |
| This PR | `25 passed`; with the K2 Horizon tool parser tests `52 passed`; all of `tests/reasoning` `492 passed`; pre-commit passes |

**Tool call with an end tag in its argument, real tokenizer.** The real K2 Horizon tokenizer and `ParserManager.get_parser(tool_parser_name="k2_horizon", reasoning_parser_name="k2_horizon", enable_auto_tools=True)`, with a tool call `echo` whose argument is `a </ifm|think> b`. Correct means `reasoning == "plan"` and the call `echo({"text": "a </ifm|think> b"})` is parsed. Each output runs through `parse`, `parse_delta` with all tokens in one delta, and `parse_delta` one token at a time.

| Output | effort | `main` | First commit | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `plan` + tool call | `high` | wrong: non-streaming, one delta | wrong: non-streaming, one delta | correct |
| `plan` + tool call | `medium`, `low` | correct | wrong: non-streaming, one delta | correct |
| `plan</ifm\|think>` + tool call | `high` | correct | correct | correct |
| `plan</ifm\|think>` + tool call | `medium`, `low` | wrong: all three | correct | correct |

In every "wrong" case the tool call is lost: reasoning runs into the tool block, and nothing is parsed as a call.

**Replay of real model output on `main`.** 120 raw K2-Horizon-7B generations, recorded with `/v1/completions` on a prompt rendered by the chat template (`skip_special_tokens=False`, temperature 1.0, prompts "你是谁？" and "Who are you?", 20 per row), replayed with the real tokenizer through the same composed parser: `parse` for non-streaming, `parse_delta` one token at a time for streaming.

| effort | tools | correct, non-streaming (before → after) | correct, streaming (before → after) |
|---|---|---|---|
| low | none | 15 → 20 | 15 → 20 |
| low | 1 function | 20 → 20 | 20 → 20 |
| medium | none | 0 → 20 | 0 → 20 |
| medium | 1 function | 0 → 20 | 0 → 20 |
| high | none | 17 → 17 | 17 → 17 |
| high | 1 function | 20 → 20 | 20 → 20 |

The 3 `high` outputs that are not correct are the same before and after: 2 have no end tag at all (the case #60969 is about), and 1 is a degenerate generation with a second `</ifm|think>` inside its answer. Streaming and non-streaming disagree on 47 of 120 outputs before this PR and on 2 after (those 2 `high` outputs with no end tag). The earliest-boundary commit leaves this table unchanged: 3 of the 120 outputs (and none of 40 more recorded with a system prompt) contain `<ifm|tool_calls>`, and all 3 close their thinking first.

**End to end** (vLLM 0.31.0 + vllm-metal on an Apple M5 with an MLX 4-bit conversion of the model; the 0.31.0 parser file is identical to `main` before this PR, and the patch in #62743 makes the same change as the first commit against 0.31.0): 240 `/v1/chat/completions` requests, `medium`/`low` × streaming/non-streaming × with/without tools, plus `high`. For `medium`/`low`, 91 of 160 responses were split wrongly before (45 with the answer in `reasoning`, 46 with the reasoning and end tag in `content`) and 0 after. 5 of 160 still have a tag in `content`: their reasoning was split correctly, but the model then emitted a second `</ifm|think>` (4) or a stray `<ifm|tool_calls>` block (1) later in its answer at temperature 1.0. `high`: 73 → 76 of 80 correct; the rest hit `max_tokens` while still thinking. Full tables and a `curl` reproducer are in #62743. This run used the first commit and was not repeated. The second commit only changes outputs in which `<ifm|tool_calls>` comes before an end tag, and none of the 160 recorded raw outputs do.

Not run on CUDA or with bf16 weights. The parser is pure Python, and the checks above use the real tokenizer and special tokens.

## Details

Root cause, part 1: `_EFFORT_TOKENS` maps each effort to one start/end pair, and every boundary check (`_split_model_output`, the streaming buffer search and its partial-tag hold-back, `is_reasoning_end`, `is_reasoning_end_streaming`, `extract_content_ids`) looked only for that effort's end tag. The chat template opens `medium` thinking with `<ifm|think_fast>` and `low` with `<ifm|think_faster>`, but in raw runs the model closed `medium` thinking with `</ifm|think>` 40 of 40 times, and tool-less `low` thinking 5 of 20 times. The parser then never saw an end.

Root cause, part 2 (found in review, thanks @adenzhou1350): `_split_model_output`, the streaming buffer and `extract_content_ids` checked for an end tag before looking for `<ifm|tool_calls>`. An end tag inside a tool call that started earlier therefore won whenever both were in the text being checked: in non-streaming and in a multi-token delta, but not when streaming one token at a time, which stops at the tool-call start. On `main` only the requested effort's own end tag could trigger this (in the review example, `</ifm|think>` under `high`); accepting all three end tags made `</ifm|think>` trigger it under `medium`/`low` too.

Fix: `_END_TOKENS` (the three end tags) and `_end_token_ids` are accepted as ends of reasoning whatever the effort. `_find_boundary` returns the earliest of them and `<ifm|tool_calls>`: content starts after an end tag, or at the tool-call start, which stays in the content. `_split_model_output` and the streaming buffer use it, and `extract_content_ids` does one forward scan that stops at the first end-token id or tool-call-start id. `is_reasoning_end` scans backwards and already returns `True` for either boundary. The start token stays per effort because the template emits it. `end_token` and `reasoning_end_str` still return the effort's own tag, so anything that inserts an end tag keeps using the one the template expects. Unchanged from `main`: `is_reasoning_end_streaming` does not treat `<ifm|tool_calls>` as an end.

Relation to #60969: that PR makes non-streaming return output with no boundary as `reasoning` with `content: null`, matching streaming. Without this fix, `medium`/`low` output closed by `</ifm|think>` has no recognised boundary, so #60969 alone would also move the whole answer into `reasoning` for non-streaming requests. The two PRs change different lines and can land in either order: a three-way merge of both files is clean, and the merged test file passes (26 tests). With both, unfinished output is reasoning and finished output is split correctly.

Not a duplicate: I searched issues and PRs for "K2 Horizon", "k2_horizon", "ifm|think" and "think_fast". #60969 handles output with no end tag. #55195 is about multi-token deltas in `BaseThinkingReasoningParser`, whose streaming path K2 Horizon overrides. #57768 adds regex timeouts to the K2 Horizon tool parser.

AI assistance: Claude Code wrote both commits, the tests, the replay and boundary-check scripts and this description, and ran the measurements on my machine. I reviewed every changed line and the results above.

Independent component check on `8e4b43e`: your 19 tests pass. I found an implicit-boundary regression with `medium`/`low` and `plan<ifm|tool_calls><ifm|tool_call>ping{"text":"</ifm|think>"}</ifm|tool_call></ifm|tool_calls>`. The parent keeps `plan` as reasoning and the tool block intact. This head instead splits at the later `</ifm|think>` inside the tool text. Characterwise streaming still gives the original split, while a single delta does not. Could the earlier implicit tool boundary take precedence over a later explicit end?

[Reproduction and scope](https://github.com/adenzhou1350/kernel_opt_agent/blob/15a27f292d69867fd3d12405290956c0ba157a5e/examples/native-k2-reasoning-boundary/README.md): same 21-test inventory on both arms; the parent fails your two expected cross-effort cases, this head fixes them but fails the two added boundary checks. Thanks for the detailed repro. You're right—the parser currently gives an explicit end tag precedence over an earlier tool boundary, which can corrupt the split when a tool argument contains an end tag and make the result depend on chunking.

I'll update the text and token-ID extraction paths to select the earliest boundary, preserving the tool marker and everything after it when that boundary comes first. I'll also add regression coverage for non-streaming and multiple streaming partitions, while retaining coverage for explicit ends that precede tool calls.
